main_text.head: EXERCITATIO PRIMA PRÆLIMINARIS, DE THEOLOGIA NATURALI.
SUMMARIUM.

p.i: I. Theologiæ Naturalis studium præ aliis homine dignum. II. Menti humanæ in statu unionis difficillimum. III. Periculi quoque plenum; ideoque tractandum reverenter. IV. Naturalis de Deo notitia maximè practica est. V. Minimè tamen ad æternam beatitatem sufficiens. VI. Non confundenda cum Fidei revelatione. VII. Interim hujus illi habenda ratio. VIII. Naturalis Theologia Revelatæ utilissima. IX. Ejus certitudo summa, si ritè tradatur.

main_text.p: I. Theologiæ Naturalis studium præ aliis homine dignum.Ti rebus omnibus, ita imprimis ratione gaudentibus, is quo feruntur ad consequendum sibi maximam quam possunt sui perfectionem, congenitus est impetus. Partem ejus haud minimam absolvit in homine quâ is omnis natura scire desiderat cupiditas. Hanc itaque nisi pro viribus satiare laboret, quanto hac parte existit negligentior, tanto magis indignis modis infra suam sortem semet ipsum abjice-
Note: the initial word "Ti" is the large woodcut initial "U" of "Cum" or similar; the first word reads as printed "Ti rebus" with the initial letter unreadable [?].

page.notes: The large initial letter is a woodcut; its letter is uncertain (taken as "U" [?]), so the first word is given as printed "Ti" with doubt. Side note text in the right margin is set in italic and is copied as printed. The text is in a Latin theological treatise; the first line of the body reads "Ti rebus omnibus" as printed (possibly "Tu" [?]). Page number not printed.
